title: Postmortem and action plan: reservoir misallocation, KV-cache thrash and burst token-bucket rewrite
creator: Maya Patel
description: Follow-up to the dedicated-cluster capacity event on 2026-02-10 that caused elevated tail latency and tenant evictions across a subset of GPU pools. Root causes included reservoir misallocation (cold-start reservations placed on fragmented hosts), KV-cache thrash from a heavy short-lived workload, and an overly permissive burst policy that allowed sustained bursts to starve neighbours. This ticket captures the incident summary, technical findings, and an actionable plan to harden tenant isolation and burst behaviour.
postmortem_summary: On 2026-02-10 we observed a multi-tenant capacity degradation in three dedicated clusters in us-west1. Symptoms: rising 99th percentile token latency, spike in container evictions, and increased OOM/kvcache miss churn. Investigation revealed a combination of (1) a reservoir allocation algorithm that favored minimal host count during cold-start placement, resulting in uneven reservation fragmentation; (2) a client workload that generated repeated short sessions and invalidated KV cache entries, dramatically increasing memory pressure; and (3) the soft-burst token-bucket permit which allowed tenants to consume sustained additional slots for multiple minutes, leading to eviction cascades. Remediation: immediate manual rebalancing and temporary lowering of soft-burst multiplier. Long-term: implement per-tenant weighted reservoirs, KV cache TTL smoothing, and a deterministic token-bucket rewrite with decay and preemption rules.
technical_findings: Reservoir misallocation: the placement algorithm attempted to minimize host count for new reservations which concentrated small reservations on a few hosts and prevented future consolidation. This created fragmentation and limited room for bursts.
KV-cache thrash: high churn workload (many short-lived sessions) caused frequent cache invalidation and inefficient prefix reuse, increasing memory and GPU page faults.

Burst policy gap: current soft-burst policy allowed sustained bursts up to 2.5x baseline for up to 10 minutes without global fairness checks; no global token accounting across tenants on the same host.
Eviction cascade mechanism: the eviction controller used host-level thresholds without tenant-weighted priority, so heavy tenants triggered evictions impacting best-effort tenants.
Telemetry blind spots: missing per-tenant burst credits and lack of early-warning on growing reservation fragmentation hampered fast automated mitigation.
timeline: 2026-02-10 02:17 UTC - First customer report: elevated tail latency in us-west1 dedicated cluster
2026-02-10 02:28 UTC - Pager duty: SRE engaged and began triage using cluster-level dashboards
2026-02-10 02:55 UTC - Temporary mitigation: reduced soft-burst multiplier from 2.5x to 1.2x and paused non-critical scheduling
2026-02-10 04:10 UTC - Manual rebalance: moved six fragmented reservations to free hosts, decreasing eviction rate
2026-02-10 06:00 UTC - Incident declared resolved for customer-facing errors; internal follow-up opened
2026-02-12 - Begin root-cause analysis and load replay in staging to reproduce reservoir fragmentation effects

action_items: Implement per-tenant weighted reservoir allocator (owner: Sofia Ruiz, due: 2026-03-12) - ties reservations to tenant weights and prevents host concentration.
Rewrite burst controller to a shared token-bucket with decay+preemption and per-host global accounting (owner: Liam O'Connor, due: 2026-03-15) - ensures sustained bursts are throttled fairly.
Add KV-cache TTL smoothing and session-aware prefix scoring to reduce thrash (owner: Arjun Mehta, due: 2026-03-10) - reduces cache churn from short-lived sessions.
Introduce a reservation fragmentation metric and alert (owner: Maya Patel, due: 2026-02-28) - early detection of dangerous consolidation patterns.
Create automated rebalance job to defragment reservations during low-util windows (owner: Platform Autoscaler team, due: 2026-03-22) - reduces need for manual moves.
Modify eviction controller to respect tenant priority weights and protect small high-SLA tenants (owner: Reliability team, due: 2026-03-08) - reduces collateral damage from noisy workloads.
Ship dashboard panels for per-tenant burst credits, reservation distribution heatmap, and KV churn SLI (owner: Observability team, due: 2026-03-05) - improve triage speed.
Run a staged rollout of the token-bucket rewrite with canary on two non-production clusters and one dedicated commercial cluster (owner: Liam O'Connor, due: 2026-03-25) - verify behaviour under load.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant weighted reservoirs are active and unit tests + integration tests validate placement invariants
Burst controller passes chaos tests: sustained synthetic load across tenants does not exceed 1.1x baseline per-tenant allocation for >5 minutes
KV-cache smoothing reduces cache invalidation rate by >= 40% on replayed workload
Reservation fragmentation metric reported and alerting thresholds tuned; paging only on high-confidence events
Eviction events from noisy tenants reduced by >= 50% in canary clusters
notes: 2026-02-16 - Design feedback from runtime-ops: prefer deterministic decay in token bucket rather than exponential to simplify reasoning for SREs (Maya).
2026-02-18 - Security review not required for allocator changes; burst controller will be behind runtime feature flag for staged enablement (Liam).
2026-02-22 - Observability: added temporary Grafana panel 'reservation_heatmap_v2' for manual triage. Link in links section.

2026-02-25 - Engineering sync: agreed to prioritize weighted allocator and token-bucket rewrite concurrently to reduce time-to-resolution. Trade-off: live migration complexity vs faster software-only mitigations.
